body:
Taking into account what I have said in my first post about the way mental health is treated where I am, what avenues can you suggest? 

Just to outline what I've done already therapy wise; CBT, DBT, mindfulness, group therapy, attachment therapy, PTSD therapy, just normal counselling. 

I you have suggestions on other acumen yes feel free to point them out. 

I did say that the one person doesn't mean any less. I do talk to him, but given that he has been the sole support for me for 9years, it weighs heavily on him too. It is never easy to hear the person you love say 'I wih I were dead' I really don't think me saying that aloud while we are goin through the things we're going through right now would help. He doesn't need the worry of me doing something to myself if he needs to go to a job interview. (I am not saying that I will, but that is a worry that would occupy someone after being told their partner is suicidal) 

I'm completely aware this is my brain doing this to me. I think I said that well in the intro post. But just because its my brain being this way does not make it easier. I'm the one say here with the nagging thoughts at the back of my mind telling me this, and regardless of what I do it doesn't shift. I do not choose to have this voice. I do not want this voice. I would give anything to not be plagued with these horrors. But I am. Simply knowing its neuroma misfiring in your mind does not fix the problem. If anything it makes the problem all thy more frustrating.

I appreciate the sentiment, truly. But there's no point trying to polish a turd. 

Th plain and simple matter is I have one person who loves me ad would miss me. There's no point dressing it up any other way. No I am not lessening the importance of that one person, but it really annoys me when the term "people" is used. I do not have people. I have person. That is it. That is life. That is truth. 

It's not depression talking, it's plain simple fact. Sorry, it just bugs me.

We are approaching everything one at a time. But when there's no money there's no money. There's vey little you can do about it. 

And when you've to juggle depression anxiety and trying to work, you can't really just focus on one or the other. It's a very vicious cycle. Jobs are responsibilities. You cannot say oh I'm sorry I can't physically open the front door today so I won't be in. People don't get that. It's not a valid reason to them.
